chunks: Hadith 5543 — And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Ibn Miskān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, the seller of al-Sābirī cloth, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who entrusted a man with some wealth. When death approached her, she said to him: “The wealth which I gave to you belongs to so-and-so,” and then the woman died.
Then her heirs came to the man and said: “Our relative had wealth, and we only consider it to be with you, so swear to us that you have nothing belonging to her.” Should he swear to them?

He عليه السلام said: “If she was regarded as trustworthy by him, then he should swear. But if she was under suspicion, then he should not swear, and he should leave the matter upon what it was. Indeed, she only has a right to one-third of her wealth.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاؤُهَا: her heirs or legal relatives who claim her estate
key_terms.اسْتَوْدَعَتْ: entrusted or deposited property with someone for safekeeping
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death, in the context of a terminal illness or final moments
key_terms.ثُلُثُهُ: one-third, the portion of wealth a person may dispose of by will
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةً: regarded as trustworthy and reliable in her statement
key_terms.مُتَّهَمَةً: considered suspect or not fully trusted in this claim
key_terms.يَحْلِفُ: to swear an oath in response to a legal claim

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dying woman says entrusted wealth belongs to someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling concerning a dying woman’s statement about entrusted wealth and its effect on inheritance rights. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes between whether her claim is considered trustworthy or suspect, and clarifies that such a disposition is limited by the rule that she may only direct one-third of her wealth outside the ordinary inheritance structure.
